rationale: Registered the successor execution that removes the vote-path synthesis caveat by letting the target's own state machine produce the campaign: the harness adds a stale_campaign_wins case where one peer keeps a snapshot of the configuration in which it was still a voter, its vote is then removed in the committed configuration, every instance is stopped, and only that peer and one other are restarted while the former leader stays down. Construction-time local feedback: with the flag enabled the peer reconstructed three voters from its own snapshot while its log's committed configuration has two and grants it no vote, campaigned on its own (the other instance observed one pre-vote and one real vote request from it), was answered by that instance whose own reconstruction was empty, and became Leader; with the flag disabled it reconstructed the committed configuration, holds no vote there, never campaigned (no request reached the other instance) and stayed Follower.

scope.description: Whether a peer whose reconstruction still grants it a vote, but whose committed configuration does not, can campaign on its own and acquire leadership with support from a peer that also reconstructs a configuration. Seventeen in-process cases: the fifteen previously exercised restart shapes plus a stale_campaign_wins case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case one peer snapshots itself while still a voter, its vote is removed in the committed configuration, all instances are stopped, and only that peer and one other are restarted while the former leader stays down.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transports and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; both rebuilt instances are reconnected to each other in both directions.
The former leader is deliberately left down so that neither rebuilt instance knows a leader and the known-leader rejection cannot mask the vote path.

The peer that campaigns holds a snapshot of the configuration in which it was still a voter and a tracked commit index that covers the configuration entry removing its vote, which is what the flag-enabled reconstruction reads instead.

The other instance holds no snapshot of its own, so its flag-enabled reconstruction is empty; the campaign is entirely produced by the target's own state machine and delivered over the real transport.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, pre-vote-only campaigns without a following real election, membership changes during the window, and any claim about what a full restored cluster would decide afterwards.

experiment.prefix: The new case builds a three-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 3, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), applies 20 commands, has one non-leader peer take its own snapshot through the public API while it is still a voter, records that snapshot's configuration index and voter count, then calls leader.DemoteVoter for that peer and applies ten more entries. It reads the peer's own log configuration entry, voter count, member and vote status and tracked commit index and emits a campaign_inputs CA_EVENT, stops every instance, rebuilds only that peer and the third peer over their own stores with the case flag, reconnects them to each other, registers an observer on the third peer for incoming pre-vote and vote requests, waits up to 1500 ms for the campaigning peer to become leader, and emits a campaign_result CA_EVENT with both peers' reconstructed voter counts, the peer's vote status in its own committed configuration, whether it became leader, its final state and how many pre-vote and vote requests the third peer received.
experiment.responsibility: runFollower and runCandidate decide whether the node campaigns and how many grants it needs, and requestVote on the answering peer decides whether to grant, so a reconstructed configuration that grants the node a vote it does not have lets leadership be acquired with support the committed configuration does not sanction.

comparisons.description: Campaign case with the flag enabled: a peer that holds no vote in the configuration recorded in its own log is not expected to acquire leadership.
Control: with the flag disabled the same peer reconstructs the committed configuration, holds no vote there and does not campaign.
Campaign case with the flag enabled: whether the campaigning peer's real vote request reached the other instance in this execution.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds the stale_campaign_wins case with its flag-disabled control, in which the campaign is produced by the peer's own reconstruction rather than by a delivered request: the peer holds a snapshot of the configuration in which it was a voter, loses its vote in the committed configuration, and is restarted together with one other peer while the former leader stays down. Replaces the comparison set with the leadership predicate and the delivered-request predicate.
